item.title: 95 to 105 Whetstone Road, 16th August
item.description:
The stretch of road between 95 and 105 Whetstone Road, extending through Farjeon Road to the main road at Charlton Park Lane, has not been cleaned for over three months. This area was once kept clean, but it has now become extremely dirty and unsightly. Rubbish is regularly dropped by people using the nearby shops and by children, with waste accumulating on street corners, pavements, and pathways. The amount of litter is unacceptable and presents a health and environmental concern. The build-up of dry rubbish also increases the risk of fire, particularly during warm weather. I request that this area be cleaned urgently and placed on a regular street-cleaning schedule.
Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Whetstone Road, Kidbrooke

item.title: Pathway mouldy and leaking water, 16th August
item.description:
I am writing to make an urgent complaint regarding a Thames Water gully/sewer cover that has been leaking sewage water continuously for over two months. Despite the issue being reported, no repairs have been carried out. A representative from Greenwich Council has attended the location and marked the ground, indicating that the problem has been identified. However, the leak remains unresolved and sewage-contaminated water continues to flow onto the public footpath. As a result, stagnant water and mould have formed on the pavement, creating an extremely dangerous slip hazard. This morning, a person pushing a baby pram slipped on the mould-covered surface after stepping into the standing water and fell. Fortunately, the child was not seriously injured, but this incident highlights the immediate danger to the public. This situation is unacceptable. The ongoing sewage leak presents: A serious public health risk due to sewage contamination. A significant slip hazard caused by mould and standing water. A danger to pedestrians, particularly elderly people, children, wheelchair users, and parents with pushchairs. I request that Thames Water treat this as an emergency and: Attend the site immediately to stop the sewage leak. Repair the defective gully/sewer cover without further delay. Clean and disinfect the affected footpath. Remove the mould and restore the pavement to a safe condition. Confirm when the repair will be completed. If this matter is not addressed urgently, I will escalate my complaint to the Consumer Council for Water (CCW), Ofwat, and the London Borough of Greenwich's Environmental Health department, as the continued failure to repair this defect is placing members of the public at risk.
Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Wricklemarsh Road, Kidbrooke
Report on FixMyStreet
